04 / 28Practice
TRU / DAY 4 / 1. Recognize when lender help would be useful

Connect the lender conversation to a specific need

A useful recommendation begins with what the buyer wants to understand.

Understand the reason

“What would you need to know before deciding whether buying fits your plans?” Listen for the question instead of assuming they want to buy now.

Explain the purpose

“A loan officer can help you understand the payment and what would need to happen next. Would that information help you plan?”

Respect their relationship

Ask about a lender they already work with. Offer an introduction when useful and accepted. A buyer can choose to keep their current lender.

What would you clarify about the buyer’s financing?

A buyer says, “My bank gave me a letter, so I’m ready to offer tonight.”

  1. What do you know from that statement?
  2. What would you ask the loan officer to confirm?
Write your practice notes
After your answer: review the explanation
Ask what the lender has reviewed, what is still conditional, whether the property affects the review, and what timing the file can support. Let the loan officer confirm the process for this buyer. Avoid promising approval, credit impact or a closing date.
08 / 28Discuss
TRU / DAY 4 / 2. Know what to explain and what the lender must confirm

Pre-qualification, pre-approval, and final approval

These are different stages. Ask what has actually been checked.

Pre-qualification

Zillow describes this as an estimate using self-reported information and a soft credit check. Ask what the buyer has actually completed.

Pre-approval

The lender reviews supporting information and identifies conditions. Ask the loan officer what has been verified and what remains before relying on the letter.

Final approval

The lender must resolve the remaining borrower and property requirements. A pre-approval letter does not guarantee funding. Confirm readiness and timing with the loan officer.

Zillow Home Loans FAQ, reviewed September 16, 2026. Ask the lender to explain credit inquiries for this buyer before they proceed.

09 / 28Train
TRU / DAY 4 / 2. Know what to explain and what the lender must confirm

Questions for the loan officer

Know which questions need a loan officer’s answer.

Before the buyer proceeds

“What will you review at this step? Will it involve a soft or hard inquiry, and what should the buyer expect afterward?”

Before relying on a letter

“What has been verified? What documents or conditions remain? Does this property change the review or payment?”

Before committing to timing

“What can you support on this file, and what do you need first?” Give the buyer the confirmed answer rather than a general estimate.

Responding to common concerns

Listen first. Answer the concern. Keep the choice with the buyer.

“I already have a lender.”

Acknowledge the relationship. Learn whether anything is still unclear.

“I don’t want a credit hit.”

Understand the concern. Let the loan officer explain the actual process before the buyer decides.

“Are you making me use them?”

The buyer chooses. An introduction is available if it helps.

15 / 28Train
TRU / DAY 4 / 3. Offer an introduction and understand concerns

Explain the reason before asking for an introduction

Fictional buyer: Jordan wants to understand payment options before deciding on the next step.

“You said the monthly payment is what you need to understand. Would a conversation with a loan officer at Zillow Home Loans help you compare your options? You choose your lender. If you want the introduction, how would you prefer to connect?”

If Jordan agrees, confirm the contact method and availability. If Jordan declines, respect the answer and agree on any useful next step with their chosen lender.

16 / 28Train
TRU / DAY 4 / 3. Offer an introduction and understand concerns PRACTICE

Practice your introduction

Use Jordan’s situation. Keep it under a minute.

One model

The presenter reveals and reads the Jordan example once, with pauses.

Try it aloud

Use Jordan’s situation. Offer one useful benefit and let the buyer choose.

One correction and retry

Each agent gets a speaking turn, feedback, and a targeted retry. If the buyer declines, respect the decision and discuss their chosen next step.

Review the practice criteria
  • Reflects the buyer’s actual concern
  • Explains one relevant supported benefit
  • Asks genuine permission and preserves buyer choice
  • Names an appropriate next action and owner; confirms after consent

TRU / DAY 4 / 4. Complete the handoff and follow through DISCUSS

What would you do after an unanswered introduction?

The buyer agreed to an introduction. You sent it, but neither the buyer nor loan officer has confirmed a call.

  1. What remains incomplete?
  2. Who would you contact?
  3. What would you record and follow up on?
Write your practice notes
After your answer: review the explanation
Check that the loan officer received the introduction and confirm a workable contact time with both parties. Tell the buyer what to expect. Record permission, the next owner and the follow-up time. Sending a message alone does not confirm the handoff.
19 / 28Discuss
TRU / DAY 4 / 4. Complete the handoff and follow through

Make the introduction and confirm the call

Permission → introduction → confirmation → follow-through.

Fictional group-message example

Jordan, meet Casey, a loan officer with Zillow Home Loans.

With your permission, I’m connecting you to discuss financing options before your next offer.

Casey, Jordan is available at 3 p.m. Can you confirm whether that works and explain the next steps?

Use your approved referral workflow and the buyer’s agreed contact channel.

Before sending

Get permission and agree how to connect.

After sending

Confirm the loan officer received it and the buyer knows what to expect.

In your CRM

Record consent, owner, agreed next step, and follow-up time.
